original_question: Does there exist an infinite family of semigroup conjugacy relations that are first-order definable, that agree with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, and that form a strict chain under inclusion?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.21, as restated in §1 and §7, specifically its chain half: whether there exists an infinite set of first-order definable semigroup conjugacies that forms a chain ordered by inclusion; §7 then answers this affirmatively via Theorem 7.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right problem very closely. It correctly asks about infinitely many first-order definable semigroup conjugacies and about arranging them in a chain by inclusion. Your clause that they agree with ordinary group conjugacy on every group is exactly the paper's defining requirement for a semigroup conjugacy. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
missing_details: Make explicit that each object in the family is an equivalence relation on every semigroup; in the paper, a semigroup conjugacy is not merely any relation that happens to coincide with group conjugacy on groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

Specify the order relation globally: for conjugacies rho and sigma, rho is included in sigma when for every semigroup S and all a,b in S, a rho b implies a sigma b; strict inclusion means this fails to reverse for some semigroup and some pair. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

To make 'first-order definable' fully stand-alone, say that the relation is definable by a first-order formula in the language of semigroups. The paper uses that phrase in §1 and §7 but does not restate the language there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

If you want a strict chain, say explicitly that the conjugacies are pairwise distinct and linearly ordered by the above inclusion relation; the official wording is 'an infinite set ... that forms a chain ordered by inclusion.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
Clarify that the question is about a family of conjugacy notions across all semigroups, not about conjugacy classes inside one fixed semigroup. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite set of pairwise distinct first-order definable semigroup conjugacies—that is, equivalence relations on semigroups, each definable by a first-order formula in the language of semigroups and coinciding with ordinary group conjugacy whenever the semigroup is a group—such that these conjugacies form a chain under the global inclusion order, meaning that for any two of them one is included in the other and inclusion is interpreted across all semigroups? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
justification: The draft is targeting the chain half of Problem 6.21. Section 1 states that Problem 6.21 asks for an infinite set of first-order definable conjugacies forming either a chain or an antichain under inclusion, and §7 repeats that formulation before proving the chain result in Theorem 7.1. Section 2 supplies the hidden formal content your draft leaves implicit: what a semigroup conjugacy is and how inclusion between conjugacies is defined. This is not the §8 construction, because §8 explicitly says those are only first-order definable relations that agree with group conjugacy on groups but are not, in general, transitive, so they are not semigroup conjugacies. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
